theme: Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Copenhagen, Prague, Lisbon, Athens, Florence, Venice, Dublin STR datasets and city-report data appendices

candidates.name: airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Python 3.4+ scraper (PostgreSQL 9.5+/PostGIS schema in postgresql/schema_current.sql) built by Tom Slee, one of the pre-Inside-Airbnb academics who ran multi-city Airbnb surveys 2015-2017 across dozens of world cities. Repo itself ships no committed data files -- it is code to run your own survey against airbnb.com. Author states 'no longer maintaining this script'; last documented release v3.6, July 2019.
candidates.why_useful: Historical precedent for pre-Inside-Airbnb multi-city Airbnb census methodology; the original Tom Slee survey outputs (not in this repo) covered some European cities circa 2015-16, which would sit inside gap #1 (archives older than Inside Airbnb's ~1yr CDN window) if located separately. As shipped, this is a live-scrape method against airbnb.com itself and out of scope to run under our rules -- catalogue only.
candidates.geography: Global, historically included multiple EU cities (city list not in this repo)
candidates.time_coverage: Tool built/used circa 2014-2019; no data range committed in-repo

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: dbt + Python data pipeline (src/extract.py, src/listings.py, src/kaggle_data.py, src/load.py, dbt/ models, Metabase dashboards) that pulls listings from insideairbnb.com/get-the-data.html at run time plus 'World Cities Population and Location' and Numbeo cost-of-living Kaggle datasets, loading into Snowflake. README claims 'over 35 million records from 2015-2020' but no CSV/parquet is committed to the repo (confirmed via file tree) -- src/listings.py scrapes whatever city list Inside Airbnb currently publishes on its get-the-data page, so it inherits Inside Airbnb's live/current-only limitation, not a frozen historical archive.
candidates.why_useful: Illustrates a reusable Inside-Airbnb-to-warehouse pipeline pattern, but does not itself supply the pre-2023 archived dumps we are missing (gap #1) since it scrapes the live page, not a historical mirror.
candidates.geography: Whatever cities Inside Airbnb currently lists (global)
candidates.time_coverage: Run-time dependent; README references 2015-2020 scope from when it was last executed, not committed data
candidates.size_hint: No data committed to repo; described historical run was ~35M rows across all Inside Airbnb cities
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing Inside Airbnb holdings; adds no new time depth or cities

candidates.name: Airbnb Prices in European Cities (Kaggle mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Kaggle-hosted mirror of the academic Gyodi & Nawaro (2021, 'Determinants of price in the sharing economy: An analysis of Airbnb data') scrape: per-city weekday/weekend CSVs for roughly 10 European cities including Amsterdam, Athens, Berlin, Lisbon and Vienna from our target list (plus Barcelona, Budapest, London, Paris, Rome), collected Aug 2018 and Jan 2019, with columns for price (realSum), room_type, person_capacity, host_is_superhost, distance to city centre/metro, cleanliness/satisfaction ratings, and weekday/weekend flag. Original source is an academic Mendeley Data deposit (exact DOI/ID not independently verified this session -- a direct Mendeley URL guess 404'd, so only the Kaggle mirror is confirmed reachable).
candidates.why_useful: One of the only multi-city academic-grade Airbnb price panels that actually covers five of our ten target cities (Amsterdam, Athens, Berlin, Lisbon, Vienna) simultaneously with a consistent methodology and hedonic covariates -- useful as an older, independent cross-check on relative ADR/price levels across those markets even though it predates our current window (2018-19 vintage, one-time weekday/weekend cut, not a time series).
candidates.geography: Amsterdam, Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Budapest, Lisbon, London, Paris, Rome, Vienna
candidates.time_coverage: Two snapshots: August 2018 and January 2019 (weekday/weekend each)
candidates.size_hint: ~51,000 listing-rows across the 10 cities per public description
candidates.license: Kaggle dataset licence not independently confirmed this session
candidates.last_activity: Underlying academic collection 2018-2019; Kaggle mirror upload date not confirmed
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Distinct vintage/methodology from our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel and our 123-market reviews-based stays index; not previously catalogued

candidates.name: GitHub topic: short-term-rental (survey page, not a single repo)
candidates.what_it_holds: Topic-tag listing surfacing STR-adjacent repos: Kamra-PMS (open-source hotel/STR property-management system), RentTools.io (Airbnb/Booking.com calendar sync tool), several Airbnb-scraper and MCP-agent projects (HasData/airbnb-mcp, everythingscraper/airbnb-scraper claiming occupancy/ADR/RevPAR extraction via Apify), and rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations (San Francisco peer-to-peer rental housing-market impact analysis). No committed multi-city European STR dataset found among the ~20 repos surveyed.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the current landscape of STR tooling repos is dominated by generic commercial scrapers/PMS software rather than city-specific European STR datasets; the everythingscraper/airbnb-scraper (claims ADR/RevPAR/occupancy extraction) is the only entry that, if it worked and were run against non-prohibited sources, would speak to gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) -- but it scrapes airbnb.com directly, which is out of scope for us to run.
candidates.last_activity: varies; topic page reflects current top repos as of Sep 2026

candidates.name: Dublin Inquirer GitHub org (checked, no STR registry repo found)
candidates.what_it_holds: Verified: this org (Dublin's investigative local newspaper, known for reporting on Ireland's Register of Short-Term Lettings) has only 4 public repos -- dublininquirer-com (site code), counciltracker-ie (council motions/votes tracker, forked from civictech-ie), you-draw-it (D3/TypeScript interactive-prediction visualization tool), and voter-guide-2024. No Airbnb/STR-register scraper or dataset is publicly on this org despite their STR reporting.
candidates.why_useful: Negative result worth recording so a future scout does not re-check the same lead: the Irish Register of Short-Term Lettings does not have a public GitHub scraper/mirror under this org. counciltracker-ie (forked from civictech-ie) may be worth a separate regulatory-tooling look for other Irish civic-data trackers, but it is not STR-specific.

notes: This session hit a near-total web-search tooling outage for this scout's slot: the WebSearch tool reported its session budget already exhausted (0/200 used by me -- consumed entirely by other concurrent scouts before my first call), duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com were unreachable (ECONNREFUSED, likely blocked at the network layer), ecosia.org and mojeek.com returned 403, and Bing loaded pages but silently ignored query parameters / truncated multi-word queries (returned generic tourism or unrelated dictionary/film results regardless of the actual search string) -- this looks like a broken or cached search-results proxy rather than genuine Bing output, worth flagging to whoever runs this sweep since it will have silently starved every scout using the Bing fallback this session. gh search repos also hit the shared 5,000/hr GitHub API rate limit after only 2-3 calls (shared across all concurrent scouts), and GitHub's own /search web endpoint 429'd on essentially every attempt (Retry-After 3600) even though plain repo and /topics/ pages fetched fine. Given these constraints I fell back to direct WebFetch of specific repo/org/topics pages using domain knowledge of likely candidates (Tom Slee's scraper, Inside-Airbnb-adjacent pipelines, the Dublin Inquirer STR-register angle, the Gyodi/Nawaro European hedonic-pricing dataset) rather than broad keyword discovery. Net result: I found no committed, city-specific historical STR dataset on GitHub for Amsterdam/Berlin/Vienna/Copenhagen/Prague/Lisbon/Athens/Florence/Venice/Dublin beyond what we already hold -- the numerous single-city 'Amsterdam airbnb' / 'Berlin airbnb' repos gh search surfaced were uniformly personal EDA/ML-tutorial notebooks re-analysing a single Inside-Airbnb-style snapshot CSV with no new time depth, which the brief explicitly asks me to exclude (I list none of them as candidates). RECOMMENDATION for whoever re-runs or reassigns this theme: retry with a working search backend (WebSearch once its budget resets, or gh search once the shared GitHub rate limit resets in ~1hr) and specifically target (a) municipal open-data portals for Amsterdam (data.amsterdam.nl vacation-rental permits), Berlin (Zweckentfremdungsverbot registration), Vienna (Kurzzeitvermietung), Copenhagen/Denmark's national STR platform, and Lisbon's RNAL/Alojamento Local registry -- none of which I could reach given the tooling outage -- and (b) Italy's national CIN short-term-rental identifier registry (launched 2024, covers Florence and Venice) which is a very plausible GitHub-mirrored open-data target I was unable to search for.
